domain: V178.1 VPS provider security & client data sovereignty (A-E + legal)
method: WebSearch result summaries only; generic queries; no repo/host/client data sent; nothing installed or tested. 'currentVpsFit' statements are derived ONLY from the coordinator's MEASURED FACTS (OpenStack Nova KVM/QEMU guest, SeaBIOS, no SEV/SNP/TDX flags, no /dev/sev-guest, no /dev/tdx_guest, no vTPM, plain ext4, no swap, lockdown/IMA/EVM interfaces present, journald logs). No compatibility with the current VPS is asserted beyond those facts.
threatModelSummary: On a conventional KVM guest the hypervisor operator (provider) can read guest RAM (memory dumps), boot rescue images, attach the disk, use the console and snapshot disks. Encryption at rest and in-guest sandboxes do not stop a malicious host at runtime. Only (a) hardware confidential computing (SEV-SNP/TDX/CCA, with attestation, still with known attacks) or (b) never giving the server plaintext/keys (client-side processing) change that.

signals.title: Hypervisor can dump guest memory: libvirt 'virsh dump --memory-only' / QEMU dump-guest-memory
signals.claim: Host-side tooling documented by Red Hat/IBM writes the guest's memory and CPU register state to an ELF/kdump file; QEMU also ships a GDB script to extract guest memory from a qemu process core. Hence anything in guest RAM (decrypted data, LUKS master key, age/SQLCipher keys, model prompts, KV cache) is readable by the host operator on a non-confidential VM.
signals.measuredOrClaimed: DOCUMENTED capability (whether this provider uses it is NOT known)
signals.currentVpsFit: APPLIES: current VPS is a KVM/QEMU guest without memory encryption.
signals.relevanceToODG: Foundational: no in-guest measure makes plaintext-in-RAM secret from the provider.
signals.risks: Docs are older RHEL 6/7 releases; capability persists in current libvirt (not re-verified).

signals.title: Cold-boot / in-RAM key exposure: disk-encryption keys stay in memory while mounted
signals.claim: Princeton (USENIX Security 2008) showed disk-encryption keys reside in RAM while volumes are mounted and can be recovered from memory images (AES keys reconstructable even with ~10% bit decay). Combined with SEC-A1, a hypervisor obtains the same keys without any physical attack.
signals.measuredOrClaimed: MEASURED (paper, physical machines); VM inference = reasoning from SEC-A1
signals.currentVpsFit: APPLIES.
signals.relevanceToODG: Explains why LUKS/fscrypt on this VPS protect only against offline disk/snapshot theft, not a runtime hypervisor operator.
signals.risks: None for ODG beyond correct framing; do not market disk encryption as provider-proof.

signals.title: LUKS + Network-Bound Disk Encryption (Clevis/Tang)
signals.claim: Clevis client + Tang server let LUKS volumes unlock automatically at boot only when the Tang server is reachable; Tang is stateless and needs no TLS/auth; clevis luks bind/list/report/regen/unbind documented; dracut needed for early-boot unlock; Oracle warns a Tang on a public IP lets anyone on the Internet unlock the disk.
signals.license: GPL-3.0 (Clevis/Tang, from general knowledge - UNVERIFIED in this run)
signals.hardware: none special; Tang server must be off-provider and access-restricted
signals.currentVpsFit: NOT PRESENT (root fs plain ext4). Converting root fs = reinstall/rescue-mode re-encryption (root, high-risk, owner-gated). A separate LUKS data volume/file is less disruptive (root).
signals.relevanceToODG: Protects disk images, snapshots, backups and decommissioned virtual disks against offline reading; NOT against the live hypervisor (SEC-A1/A2).
signals.risks: Provider sees the Tang exchange endpoint metadata; mis-exposed Tang = auto-unlock for anyone; boot dependence on network.

signals.title: Application-level/client-side encryption primitives: age, libsodium secretstream & sealed boxes
signals.claim: age v1: X25519 (or scrypt) recipients wrap a 128-bit file key; recent versions add mlkem768x25519 post-quantum recipients. libsodium: crypto_secretstream (XChaCha20-Poly1305, chunked streams, since 1.0.14), sealed boxes (anonymous public-key encryption to a recipient), KDF/HKDF for subkey derivation.
signals.license: age BSD-3-Clause; libsodium ISC (general knowledge - UNVERIFIED in this run)
signals.currentVpsFit: Usable now without root. Provider-proof ONLY if data is encrypted on the client side and never decrypted on the VPS (storage/relay role). Any processing on the VPS (OCR, embedding, LLM) needs plaintext + key in VPS RAM -> visible to provider (SEC-A1).
signals.relevanceToODG: Per-tenant public keys: VPS can ingest/store client blobs it cannot read (sealed boxes / age recipients whose private key is client/owner-held), and crypto-shred per tenant.
signals.risks: Contradiction with 'process client docs on the VPS': encryption-in-use is impossible here; key custody and loss = data loss.

signals.title: Envelope encryption with external KMS / Vault-OpenBao: Shamir split, auto-unseal, recovery keys
signals.claim: Vault key hierarchy: data keyring <- root key <- unseal key; default seal splits unseal key with Shamir (threshold of shares); auto-unseal via HSM/cloud KMS/Transit returns recovery keys that only authorise operations and cannot decrypt the root key. OpenBao RFC proposes multiple prioritised seals (Transit, then Shamir fallback) - proposal status not verified.
signals.license: Vault BUSL-1.1 (non-OSI, general knowledge - UNVERIFIED); OpenBao MPL-2.0 (general knowledge - UNVERIFIED)
signals.hardware: optional HSM (PKCS#11) for root of trust
signals.currentVpsFit: A KMS running ON this VPS gives no protection against the provider (keys in its RAM). Value comes from an EXTERNAL KMS/HSM (owner premises or another trust domain) that releases data keys only per request, with audit + revocation. Even then, released data keys and plaintext are in VPS RAM while in use.
signals.relevanceToODG: Rotation/revocation/recovery pattern: per-tenant KEK in external KMS, DEK per document, Shamir-split owner recovery; revoke KEK = crypto-shred tenant.
signals.risks: Availability dependency on external KMS; license choice (Vault BUSL vs OpenBao); new component (anti-duplication: check existing ODG agent-identity/secret handling first).

signals.title: Cryptographic erase is the sanitisation method NIST SP 800-88 Rev.2 still details (Sept 2025)
signals.claim: NIST SP 800-88r2 (final 2025-09-26, supersedes r1) replaced most technique detail with references to IEEE 2883/NSA specs, except cryptographic erase (CE), which gets focused guidance on key types and key sanitisation; CE validity has stringent preconditions (listed in the PDF, not retrieved here).
signals.hardware: none (application-level CE) / SED for drive-level CE
signals.currentVpsFit: Overwriting files on a virtual disk (thin-provisioned, snapshotted, SSD-backed) cannot be verified from the guest; crypto-shredding of per-tenant keys is the only deletion ODG can evidence itself - provided the key never reached a backup/snapshot in plaintext.
signals.relevanceToODG: Per-tenant DEK/KEK destruction as the 'verifiable deletion' mechanism for client data, embeddings and backups.
signals.risks: Key copies in RAM dumps/snapshots/backups defeat CE; preconditions must be read in the PDF.

signals.title: AMD SEV-SNP: hypervisor treated as untrusted; memory encryption + integrity (RMP) + signed attestation reports
signals.claim: AMD frames the threat model as an untrusted cloud provider; the AMD Secure Processor measures the guest and produces an attestation report (cert chain to AMD root/VCEK or VLEK) that the guest owner verifies before releasing secrets. Formal analysis (arXiv 2403.10296) treats the hypervisor as fully untrusted and reports issues in attestation properties.
signals.hardware: AMD EPYC Milan/Genoa+ host with SNP enabled in firmware + host kernel/QEMU support
signals.currentVpsFit: NOT AVAILABLE: measured no SEV/SEV-ES/SNP guest flags, no /dev/sev-guest. Cannot be enabled from inside the guest.
signals.relevanceToODG: The only path (besides client-side processing) to run OCR/embeddings/LLM on client plaintext with RAM protected from the hosting operator.
signals.risks: See SEC-B3 attacks; still trusts AMD firmware/microcode; physical attackers partially out of scope.

signals.title: Intel TDX: trust domains with quote-based attestation (DCAP); multiple 2025-2026 advisories
signals.claim: Intel advisories cover TDX DCAP Quote Verification Library (CVE-2025-35987, INTEL-SA-01421), TDX data-authenticity issue allowing info disclosure from the hypervisor (CVE-2025-31356, INTEL-SA-01419, fixed in 2026.2 IPU), TDX Workload Attestation cert-validation flaw (CVE-2026-42067, INTEL-SA-01520). Intel/Microsoft joint TDX 1.5 review reported an 'attestation forgery via migration' finding; Intel refreshed SGX/TDX CRLs after TEE.fail research.
signals.measuredOrClaimed: OFFICIAL_ADVISORIES (dates in search summaries partly inconsistent - verify on Intel pages)
signals.hardware: Intel Xeon (Sapphire Rapids+/Emerald Rapids/Granite Rapids) with TDX enabled + TDX module + host stack
signals.currentVpsFit: NOT AVAILABLE: no /dev/tdx_guest measured.
signals.relevanceToODG: Alternative CVM technology; attestation verification must pin TCB levels and refresh CRLs.
signals.risks: Attestation verifier software itself had CVEs; patch-level (TCB) policy is mandatory.

signals.title: Published attacks on SEV-SNP/TDX: CacheWarp, BadRAM, Heracles, Battering RAM, attestation forgery (Mior/Skyfall)
signals.claim: CacheWarp (USENIX Sec 2024, CVE-2023-20592): software fault injection reverting guest cache lines on SEV-ES/SNP, microcode fix. BadRAM (Dec 2024, CVE-2024-21944/AMD-SB-3015): physical SPD tampering (~cheap hardware) to fake attestation and backdoor SEV VMs; firmware fix + SPD lock. Heracles (CCS 2025): chosen-plaintext via deterministic re-encryption on page relocation; AMD mitigations. Battering RAM (Oct 2025): interposer bypassing BadRAM mitigations, affects Intel and AMD memory encryption. CSA note reports CVE-2026-0462 / AMD-SB-3059 attestation-measurement forgery with hypervisor+BIOS+PCIe device control (secondary source). AMD declined mitigation for an aliasing issue (AMD-SB-3024) as outside its threat model.

evidence.type: secondary research note - UNVERIFIED vs AMD bulletin

signals.measuredOrClaimed: MEASURED (academic attacks); patch status per vendor bulletins NOT re-verified
signals.currentVpsFit: n/a (no CVM).
signals.relevanceToODG: CVM reduces but does not eliminate provider risk; attestation policy must require minimum firmware/TCB versions; physical-access attacks remain the provider's datacenter risk.
signals.risks: Over-claiming 'provider cannot access' if moving to CVM - forbidden by anti-overclaim rule.

signals.title: Arm CCA (Realms/RME): specified, Linux support documented, public server silicon not confirmed
signals.claim: RME is optional from Armv9.3-A; CCA firmware open source; Linux arm64 docs describe Realm guests protected from the hypervisor. OpenCCA paper (mid-2025) states no public Arm CPU supported CCA at that time. 2026 hardware availability NOT confirmed in this run.
signals.hardware: Armv9.3-A+ with RME (no confirmed cloud offering)
signals.currentVpsFit: NOT APPLICABLE (x86 guest).
signals.relevanceToODG: Watch item only.
signals.risks: Immature ecosystem.

signals.title: OpenStack Nova 2026.2: SEV-SNP via libvirt (mem_encryption_model=amd-sev-snp), Intel TDX spec/docs
signals.claim: Nova 2026.2 (34.0.0) docs: SEV-SNP guest memory encryption requested via flavor hw:mem_encryption_model=amd-sev-snp or image hw_mem_encryption_model; host detection via /sys/module/kvm_amd/parameters/sev_snp; no live migration or suspend for SNP instances. TDX: approved spec (hw:mem_encryption_model=intel-tdx, trait HW_CPU_X86_INTEL_TDX) and admin doc; shipped status not fully confirmed.
signals.hardware: provider compute hosts with SNP/TDX-capable CPUs + firmware + recent Nova/libvirt/QEMU
signals.currentVpsFit: Upstream Nova CAN do it, but the current provider's Nova version, hardware and flavors are unknown; measured guest shows none enabled. Also SNP guests typically need OVMF/UEFI, whereas current VPS boots SeaBIOS (inference, not verified for this provider).
signals.relevanceToODG: Concrete question for the current provider: do you offer an SEV-SNP or TDX flavor (2026.2+ Nova)? Otherwise migrate.
signals.risks: Provider may run older Nova; no live migration => maintenance downtime.

signals.title: Hyperscaler CVM offerings and public prices: AWS (SNP, +10%), GCP (SNP/TDX, per-vCPU/GiB surcharge), Azure (SNP/TDX, vTPM)
signals.claim: AWS EC2: SEV-SNP on c6a/m6a/r6a sizes, only US East (Ohio) and Europe (Ireland), +10% of On-Demand hourly rate, attestation report VLEK-signed. GCP: SEV-SNP on N2D (Milan) and TDX on C3; surcharge SNP $0.0027502/vCPU-h + $0.0003686/GiB-h, TDX $0.0033982/vCPU-h + $0.0004555/GiB-h (on-demand, snippet values). Azure: confidential VMs on SEV-SNP and TDX, attested at boot, each with a vTPM.
signals.measuredOrClaimed: OFFICIAL_PRICING/DOCS (values from search snippets; re-check live pages)
signals.currentVpsFit: Would require migration.
signals.relevanceToODG: Price signal: CVM premium ~10% (AWS) or small per-vCPU/GiB adders (GCP) - not a cost blocker. But US-headquartered providers raise extraterritorial-law questions (see SEC-L2).
signals.risks: Azure SKU-level prices not collected; US providers vs sovereignty requirement.

signals.title: EU providers: IONOS Cloud offers AMD SEV-SNP Confidential VMs (EU DCs) with open-source SNPGuard attestation; OVHcloud/Scaleway/Hetzner CVM VMs NOT found
signals.claim: IONOS: Confidential VM with AMD SEV-SNP only in EU data centers with SNP hardware (tutorial uses Frankfurt-East); vCPU/RAM fixed at creation; no live migration or in-guest warm restart; SNPGuard attestation toolchain; pricing via account manager (not public). OVHcloud page found concerns bare-metal confidential computing (technology not named in excerpt). No official Scaleway or Hetzner CVM documentation found in this run.
signals.measuredOrClaimed: OFFICIAL_DOCS (IONOS); absence for others = NOT_FOUND, not proof of absence
signals.hardware: provider SNP hardware; alternatively own bare-metal AMD EPYC server with SNP enabled (owner-operated host)
signals.currentVpsFit: Would require migration.
signals.relevanceToODG: Only EU-native CVM VM offer confirmed; bare-metal EPYC rental + self-managed SNP is the other sovereignty path (provider still has physical access - SEC-B3).
signals.risks: Price opaque; follow-up needed for OVHcloud/Scaleway/Hetzner/Outscale offerings.

signals.title: Attestation is what makes a CVM meaningful: secrets released only after verifying report/quote against policy
signals.claim: AMD flow: guest measured by AMD-SP, report sent to guest owner, compared to expected measurement + policy before secrets are released. AWS documents VLEK-signed SNP reports; Azure attests SNP/TDX CVMs at boot with vTPM; Intel DCAP verifies TDX quotes (QVL with its own CVEs, CRL refresh required). Red Hat (2026) describes storage attacks where a pre-encrypted image sealed to vTPM subverts naive CVM disk trust.
signals.currentVpsFit: NOT POSSIBLE (no vTPM, no SNP/TDX report device).
signals.relevanceToODG: Key-release design for a future CVM: owner-held KMS releases tenant KEKs only to an attested measurement; attestation verifier runs OUTSIDE the provider.
signals.risks: Verifier must be off-provider and TCB-policy-pinned; measuring the full stack (kernel, initrd, cmdline) is non-trivial.

signals.title: gVisor/bwrap/Podman protect the HOST from the workload - not the workload from a malicious host
signals.claim: gVisor security model: relies on the host OS/platform for defense against hardware attacks; host kernel/hypervisor remain responsible; resource DoS protection relies on host cgroups; escape needs bugs in both Sentry and host kernel. By construction, namespace/seccomp sandboxes (bwrap, rootless Podman) run on and are fully visible to the guest kernel, which itself is visible to the hypervisor.
signals.measuredOrClaimed: DOCUMENTED (gVisor); bwrap/Podman = direct consequence of design (reasoning)
signals.currentVpsFit: APPLIES: existing bwrap sandbox gives tenant-vs-tenant and workload-vs-ODG isolation only; zero protection from provider or guest root.
signals.relevanceToODG: Must be stated in any client-facing security claim (anti-overclaim).
signals.risks: Misrepresenting sandboxing as confidentiality.

signals.title: Provider out-of-band access: OpenStack rescue mode, console, snapshots; OVHcloud VPS rescue + KVM console
signals.claim: OpenStack 'server rescue' boots a rescue image and attaches the instance's root disk for data recovery; console output/creation policies are admin_or_owner (Rocky sample); snapshot/backup commands exist. OVHcloud VPS: control-panel reboot into rescue mode with temporary password and SSH, browser KVM console (API POST /vps/{serviceName}/getConsoleUrl). Operators of the underlying cloud hold these capabilities administratively regardless of guest settings.
signals.measuredOrClaimed: DOCUMENTED (generic OpenStack + one example provider; the current VPS provider is not identified here)
signals.currentVpsFit: APPLIES (OpenStack Nova guest): plain ext4 root means rescue/snapshot gives readable disk; console gives login prompt access path.
signals.relevanceToODG: Disk encryption (SEC-A3) closes rescue/snapshot reading of data at rest; nothing closes live-RAM access.
signals.risks: Account takeover of the provider panel = same capability for an attacker: enforce MFA on provider account (owner action).

signals.title: SSH hardening reference: ANSSI 'Recommandations pour un usage sécurisé d'(Open)SSH' + post-quantum SSH transition note
signals.claim: ANSSI note DAT-NT-007 (17/08/2015) is the national SSH hardening reference, referenced by ANSSI-BP-028 Linux configuration guide v2.0 (03/10/2022); ANSSI also published a 'Transition post-quantique de SSHv2' note. Specific directives not retrieved in this run.
signals.currentVpsFit: Applicable; sshd_config changes need root (owner-gated). Current sshd settings NOT observed in this run.
signals.relevanceToODG: Key-only auth, no root login, restricted ciphers/KEX (incl. hybrid PQ KEX), AllowUsers - protects against network attackers, not against the provider console.
signals.risks: 2015 note is dated; lockout risk when changing sshd remotely (keep console path).

signals.title: Encrypted DNS: systemd-resolved DNSOverTLS=yes (strict) vs opportunistic
signals.claim: DNSOverTLS=true: all connections encrypted, server must support DoT with valid certificate; resolution fails otherwise. 'opportunistic' falls back to plaintext and cannot authenticate the server (MITM). Default off. '#hostname' SNI syntax in newer systemd; configure via drop-in in /etc/systemd/resolved.conf.d/.
signals.currentVpsFit: Applicable if VPS uses systemd-resolved (NOT observed); hides DNS queries from on-path network observers, not from the hypervisor (which sees all guest traffic and RAM).
signals.relevanceToODG: Reduces metadata leakage of internal/Radar lookups; complements egress allowlist (DNS is part of allowlist).
signals.risks: Strict mode = outage if DoT resolver unreachable; choosing a resolver is a trust decision.

signals.title: Egress filtering on the guest: netns/Landlock (rootless) + host firewall (root); provider still sees traffic
signals.claim: Per signals-E-F-G (F-01, F-03, G-02): bwrap --unshare-net removes all routes; Landlock ABI>=4 restricts TCP connect ports unprivileged. Host-level nftables/systemd IPAddressDeny need root.
signals.currentVpsFit: Rootless parts usable now (bwrap present per caller); firewall rules owner-gated.
signals.relevanceToODG: Prevents ODG/LLM pipeline from exfiltrating client data; does not address provider.
signals.risks: Guest root can disable it; provider-level network tap unaffected.

signals.title: journald hygiene: Storage=volatile|none, Seal=, retention options
signals.claim: journald Storage=volatile keeps logs only in RAM under /run/log/journal; Storage=none drops all (forwarding still works); auto = persistent iff /var/log/journal exists. Seal= (FSS) enabled by default when a sealing key exists. MaxRetentionSec definition not cleanly retrieved - check current man page.
signals.currentVpsFit: Measured: journald holds logs (persistence mode NOT stated). Changing journald.conf = root (owner-gated). Rootless alternative: ODG never logs client content (redaction at source) and runs tenant jobs with stdout/stderr captured to encrypted per-tenant files.
signals.relevanceToODG: Client text/prompt fragments in system logs would land in plaintext on ext4 disk -> readable via rescue/snapshot (SEC-D1).
signals.risks: Volatile logs lose forensic evidence after reboot - trade-off with audit requirements.

signals.title: Data-remanence surfaces for an LLM pipeline on this VPS (embeddings, caches, temp, backups, snapshots)
signals.claim: Composite recommendation from sourced pieces: embeddings and chunks in per-tenant encrypted DB (SQLCipher/SQLite3MC, see G-04), blobs with age per-tenant recipients (SEC-A4), plaintext only in tmpfs within sandbox, Ollama keep_alive=0 to unload model/KV state between tenants (G-01), no swap (measured) so RAM pages not written to disk, backups encrypted client-side before leaving VPS, deletion by key destruction (SEC-A6). Provider snapshots of the virtual disk capture whatever is on disk at that time (SEC-D1).
signals.measuredOrClaimed: PATTERN (synthesis of documented mechanisms; not tested on VPS)
signals.currentVpsFit: Achievable rootless except journald/system-level changes; protects against snapshot/rescue/backup leakage and tenant cross-contamination, NOT against live RAM access.
signals.relevanceToODG: Per-tenant cryptographic separation = one DEK per tenant, derived/wrapped by owner-held KEK.
signals.risks: Keys must be in VPS RAM to process -> provider-visible during processing; tmpfs is RAM (visible to hypervisor).

signals.title: GDPR Art. 28 processors + EDPB Guidelines 07/2020: controller must verify processor's 'sufficient guarantees'
signals.claim: EDPB Guidelines 07/2020 (v2.1 adopted 2021-07-07): controller must verify processor guarantees at appropriate intervals; contracts must not merely restate GDPR/Art. 32; with general authorisation, processor must actively notify new sub-processors. EDPB Opinion 22/2024: verification responsibility down the sub-processor chain stays with the controller. Hosting provider = (sub-)processor of client data processed by ODG.
signals.currentVpsFit: Requires the current provider's DPA (Art. 28 terms), sub-processor list and location - owner/legal action, not technical.
signals.relevanceToODG: ODG's clients (controllers) will need ODG's sub-processor chain incl. the VPS provider; technical measures (A/E) are the evidence of 'appropriate measures'.
signals.risks: Not legal advice; exact wording to be read in EDPB PDF.

signals.title: SecNumCloud 3.2 (ANSSI, 2022-03-08): adds protection against non-EU (extraterritorial) law
signals.claim: ANSSI v3.2 referential mainly adds criteria protecting against extra-European law (immunity requirements incl. corporate/shareholding structure). Qualified offers claimed by OUTSCALE, OVHcloud (hosted private cloud), Scaleway (vendor statements). A 2026 arrêté under SREN Art. 31 reported by a secondary source - NOT verified on Légifrance. CNIL has warned about EU certification schemes that would allow foreign-authority access.
signals.measuredOrClaimed: OFFICIAL_REFERENTIAL + VENDOR_CLAIMS (qualification list must be checked on ANSSI's official list)
signals.currentVpsFit: Current VPS provider qualification status UNKNOWN; a generic VPS is very unlikely to be a SecNumCloud-qualified offer (unverified).
signals.relevanceToODG: Sovereignty answer to 'provider legal access' (organisational), complementary to CVM (technical). SecNumCloud qualification ≠ confidential computing (qualified provider can still technically access RAM).
signals.risks: Qualified offers cost more and are often private-cloud, not small VPS; do not conflate qualification with CVM.

signals.title: EU Data Act (Reg. 2023/2854) cloud switching: Chapter VI applicable 2025-09-12; switching charges banned from 2027-01-12
signals.claim: Chapter VI switching provisions apply since 2025-09-12 (also to pre-existing contracts); reduced at-cost switching charges allowed until 2027-01-12, prohibited thereafter (Commission clarified this covers switching-related egress fees); max 2-month notice; transitional period generally ≤30 days.
signals.measuredOrClaimed: LEGAL_FACT per secondary sources (primary text NOT fetched)
signals.currentVpsFit: Lowers lock-in cost of migrating from the current VPS to a CVM/sovereign provider.
signals.relevanceToODG: Supports a migration plan to a confidential/sovereign host; keep infra portable (no provider-specific dependencies).
signals.risks: Applicability to small IaaS contracts/exemptions not checked.

recommendations.achievableOnThisVpsRootless: Per-tenant application-level encryption (age/libsodium for blobs, SQLCipher/SQLite3MC for DB incl. embeddings), owner-held KEK with per-tenant DEKs and crypto-shredding for deletion, bwrap netns no-egress for client jobs, tmpfs-only plaintext, Ollama keep_alive=0, no client content in logs, client-side-encrypted backups. Protects against: other tenants, compromised ODG components, network attackers, provider snapshots/rescue/backup reading of data at rest. Does NOT protect against provider runtime access to RAM.
recommendations.achievableOnThisVpsOwnerGatedRoot: LUKS data volume (optionally Clevis/Tang with an off-provider, access-restricted Tang) or full re-install with encrypted root; sshd hardening per ANSSI; systemd-resolved DoT; journald Storage=volatile or redaction policy; host egress firewall. Same limit: no protection from the hypervisor at runtime.
recommendations.requiresConfidentialComputingHost: Processing client plaintext (OCR/embeddings/LLM) with memory protected from the hosting operator requires an SEV-SNP or TDX CVM with remote attestation verified off-provider, and key release gated on attestation. Options found: IONOS Cloud SEV-SNP CVM (EU, price on request), AWS (Ireland, +10%), GCP and Azure (US-HQ providers: sovereignty trade-off), or own bare-metal AMD EPYC with SNP. Ask the current provider whether it offers Nova 2026.2 SNP/TDX flavors. Note SNP/TDX still have published attacks; require TCB-version policy.
recommendations.requiresClientSideProcessing: If no CVM: the only provider-proof option is that client documents are processed on client/owner-controlled hardware and the VPS stores/relays only ciphertext it cannot decrypt.
recommendations.legal: Obtain the provider's GDPR Art. 28 DPA + sub-processor list; check SecNumCloud qualification on ANSSI's official list if French public/sensitive clients are targeted; use Data Act switching rights for migration. Never claim 'provider cannot access data' on the current VPS.

openQuestions: Which provider/region runs the current VPS, and does it offer SEV-SNP/TDX flavors (Nova 2026.2+) or UEFI images?
Is the current VPS provider's DPA (Art. 28) and sub-processor list available; data-centre location?
IONOS CVM pricing and whether OVHcloud/Scaleway/Outscale/Hetzner offer CVM VMs (not found in this run).
Where would the owner-held KMS/attestation verifier run (owner premises? second provider?) and its availability SLA?
Current journald persistence mode, sshd config and resolver on the VPS (NOT observed).
Exact NIST SP 800-88r2 preconditions for cryptographic erase.
AMD-SB-3059 / CVE-2026-0462 official bulletin text and affected firmware (only secondary source seen).
Official ANSSI list of SecNumCloud-qualified offers and status of the 2026 SREN arrêté (unverified).
